newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Bahn pretax profit to rise 20 pct - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bahn pretax profit to rise 20 pct - magazine.

text.p: German railway Deutsche Bahn AG, boosted by the spin-off of part of its telecommunications unit, should show a 20 percent leap in 1996 pretax profit to 670 million marks ($420 million), Manager magazine said on Wednesday.
The railway would show revenue of 30.1 billion marks, up slightly from 1995, the business magazine said in an article due to appear on Friday.
A summary of the story was made available in advance. Deutsche Bahn officials were not immediately available for comment.
Without sharp gains from its DBKom unit, pretax profit would have reached only 550 million marks, unchanged from the year before, the magazine said.

Deutsche Bahn in July sold 49.8 percent of DBKom to a consortium led by Germany's Mannesmann AG. The joint company, which also includes AT&T Corp, is using DBKom's 40,000 km of phone lines along railroad tracks to build a nationwide phone network.
The joint company aims to emerge as the number two phone company after Deutsche Telekom AG in Germany's deregulated telecommunicaitons market.
Deutsche Bahn in November said it expected 1996 revenue to exceed 30 billion marks, and outlined plans for 81 billion marks in capital investments over the next three years.
In the first six months of 1996, before the sale of the DBKom stake, Deutsche Bahn's pretax profit rose 17.5 percent to 188 million marks
-- Neal Boudette, Bonn Newsroom, (49-228) 260 97 150 ($ = 1.596 German Marks)
